question: Which level of government in Nigeria is in charge of running primary health centres?
explanation: Primary health care delivery is managed by local government authorities with support from state agencies. [learn more](BMP117_U1_T8#BMP117_U1_T8_h1)

question: What is the main responsibility of the federal level in the Nigerian health system?
explanation: The federal level focuses on national policies, regulations, and high-level specialized tertiary hospitals. [learn more](BMP117_U1_T8#BMP117_U1_T8_h1)

question: What core approach does the Nigerian National Health Policy use as the foundation for health care delivery?
explanation: The national health policy builds the entire health system upon the philosophy and principles of Primary Health Care. [learn more](BMP117_U1_T8#BMP117_U1_T8_h2)

question: A midwife is setting up a new rural maternity clinic. According to the national health policy, what should guide the facility standards?

options.C: Personal preference of the community chief

explanation: Health policies establish minimum standards to ensure safety and quality across all levels of service delivery. [learn more](BMP117_U1_T8#BMP117_U1_T8_h2)

question: Which agency was established to coordinate and drive primary health care development in Nigeria?

options.B: National Agency for Food and Drug Administration
options.D: National Primary Health Care Development Agency

explanation: The NPHCDA was created to provide support and coordination for PHC implementation nationwide. [learn more](BMP117_U1_T8#BMP117_U1_T8_h3)

question: Why was the Midwives Service Scheme introduced into the Nigerian PHC implementation strategy?

options.A: To provide administrative jobs for urban health workers
options.B: To generate commercial revenue for local government councils
options.C: To reduce high maternal and child mortality in rural areas
options.D: To replace traditional birth attendants with modern surgeons

explanation: The MSS addresses severe staff shortages in rural PHC clinics to improve maternal and child survival rates. [learn more](BMP117_U1_T8#BMP117_U1_T8_h3)

question: What serves as the basic operational unit for planning and service delivery under the Ward Health System?
explanation: The Ward Health System uses the political ward as its foundational unit for community-level health organisation. [learn more](BMP117_U1_T8#BMP117_U1_T8_h4)

question: How does the Ward Health System improve maternal health care at the grassroots level?

options.A: By transferring all pregnant women to federal teaching hospitals
options.B: By banning all traditional birth attendants from rural settlements
options.C: By eliminating the need for community health extension workers
options.D: By involving the community in managing health committees to build trust

explanation: Community involvement through ward health committees fosters local ownership and encourages women to use the health facility. [learn more](BMP117_U1_T8#BMP117_U1_T8_h4)

question: Which of the following describes intersectoral collaboration in primary health care?

options.A: Sharing medical supplies between federal and state hospitals
options.B: Partnering only with international private donor agencies
options.C: Collaborating exclusively among different nursing specialties
options.D: Working with other sectors like agriculture and education

explanation: Intersectoral collaboration involves cooperation between health and non-health sectors to address the root causes of ill health. [learn more](BMP117_U1_T8#BMP117_U1_T8_h5)

question: Why is community participation considered vital for the success of PHC projects in Nigeria?

options.A: It guarantees automatic international funding for local clinics
options.B: It allows community members to replace trained midwives in theatres
options.C: It fosters a sense of local ownership and ensures long-term sustainability
options.D: It removes the financial burden of purchasing drugs from the government

explanation: When communities participate from the planning stage, they take pride in the facility and sustain its operations over time. [learn more](BMP117_U1_T8#BMP117_U1_T8_h5)

question: What is the main purpose of the Basic Health Care Provision Fund in Nigeria?

options.A: To build ultra-modern tertiary airports for sick patients
options.B: To finance a basic minimum package of health services
options.C: To purchase private luxury vehicles for health commissioners
options.D: To pay international consultants for policy writing

explanation: The BHCPF is dedicated to funding basic health services, emergency care, and facility upgrades at the primary level. [learn more](BMP117_U1_T8#BMP117_U1_T8_h6)

question: How do health insurance schemes help protect families seeking maternal care at PHC facilities?

options.A: By providing free private jets for emergency obstetric referral
options.B: By transferring hospital management entirely to commercial banks
options.C: By pooling financial risks and reducing out-of-pocket spending
options.D: By exempting insured families from following clinical guidelines

explanation: Health insurance pools funds so that families do not face sudden, unaffordable medical bills during childbirth complications. [learn more](BMP117_U1_T8#BMP117_U1_T8_h6)

question: Which of the following is NOT a major challenge facing primary health care in Nigeria?

options.A: Dilapidated physical infrastructure in rural clinics
options.B: Irregular supply of essential life-saving medicines
options.C: Acute staff shortages and professional brain drain
options.D: Excessive surplus of functioning medical equipment

explanation: PHC facilities typically suffer from a severe lack of equipment rather than a surplus, making this option incorrect. [learn more](BMP117_U1_T8#BMP117_U1_T8_h7)

question: What is the main focus of recent PHC reform efforts in the national health strategy?

options.A: Revitalising facilities and strengthening supply chains
options.B: Abolishing the primary healthcare tier in the constitution
options.C: Replacing all community midwives with automated machines
options.D: Closing down all primary health centres in rural settlements

explanation: Current reforms concentrate on facility revitalisation and ensuring essential medicines reach grassroots clinics reliably. [learn more](BMP117_U1_T8#BMP117_U1_T8_h7)
